Subject: [URGENT] Production latency & 504 spike impacting checkout (BrightCart)

Hannah / Marissa / Sean —

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95/p99 latency and 504 responses around 08:55 PT this morning. Impact: ~12% of checkout requests are timing out for users in us-west and causing a visible drop in throughput. Our stack shows many client-side retries from our checkout service which is exacerbating the problem. Attaching our Grafana p99 screenshot and a CSV of trace IDs.

Key evidence attached: brightcart_p99_dashboard_20270412.png, brightcart_client_trace_ids.csv

Immediate asks: can you confirm whether there were any infra changes or deploys on the hosted API? If not, we need Redwood to investigate whether API latency increased or if our SDK retries are amplifying transient backend delays. This is customer-facing (orders failing) — requesting an urgent postmortem and mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Alice Nguyen
Senior SRE, BrightCart
ops@brightcart.com

Subject: Re: [INVESTIGATING] Production latency & 504 spike impacting checkout (BrightCart)

Hannah / Sean —

Quick notes from initial triage (engineer on call: Connor):
- No code or infra deploys in hosted API before spike.
- Backend host latency (service-side processing) increased by ~10ms median across the board — not enough to explain the 12% failure rate.
- Large majority of the elevated p99s correlate with high retry counts from the same BrightCart checkout IP ranges and the trace IDs provided. We see repeated request IDs within ~200–800ms windows.

Preliminary hypothesis: client-side timeouts + aggressive retry policy produced retry amplification which pushed queueing behind the load balancer and led to bursts in p99/504s. BrightCart traces show the pattern: initial request times out on the client after ~500ms -> immediate retry -> second request queues -> backend responds slowly to queued requests -> client times out again -> more retries. This creates a feedback loop.

Immediate mitigations we can enact from Redwood side:
1) Soft account-level rate limit to smooth bursts (temporary)
2) Throttle retries at the edge (exponential backoff enforcement for known SDK fingerprints)
3) Provide BrightCart with recommended SDK timeout/backoff config and a patched release note.

Action items:
- Marissa: deploy temporary account throttle for BRG-3421 (BrightCart) — in progress.
- Sean: add temporary request dedupe by idempotency header where present.
- Hannah: coordinate exec communication and proposed customer credit if orders lost.

Marissa has the runbook open and will update the incident doc. I’ll prepare a concise exec summary for Rishi.

—Marissa Cole
Sr. Technical Account Manager — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Fwd: BrightCart production latency surge — executive summary and next steps

Team — forwarding a concise summary for exec attention and next steps. BrightCart is asking for an immediate estimate of impact and credits; procurement is looped.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Incident window: 08:55–09:40 PT (peak spike at ~09:02).
- Observed impact: ~12% checkout failures/504s; order throughput dip during spike.
- Root cause (prelim): retry amplification originating from BrightCart checkout service (SDK v2.8.1) configured with a 500ms timeout and 2 immediate retries. Retries produced burst traffic that increased queueing and exposed backend tail latency. There is no evidence of a Redwood code or infra deploy that caused this.
- Mitigations applied by Redwood: temporary account-level throttle for BRG-3421, edge retry-throttle measures, and request dedupe where idempotency headers exist.
- Customer asks: timeline, estimate of lost orders, customer credit.

Recommended next steps:
1) Approve a goodwill credit for impacted orders (we should quantify quickly; Marissa to provide estimate).
2) Coordinate a joint postmortem with BrightCart SREs to finalize root cause and SDK guidance.
3) Rapidly publish SDK recommended settings and push a patch to the JS SDK to implement sensible default backoff to avoid immediate retry storms.
4) Consider product changes: server-side adaptive backpressure / per-account smoothing to prevent amplification from aggressive clients.

Marissa: attaching our quick notes (redwood_quick_notes_20270412.pdf) and the BrightCart traces they sent. If you agree with the credit recommendation, propose an amount and we’ll route approval. Rishi, please advise on executive messaging and credit authority.

—Hannah
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
